set -euo pipefail cd "$TP_HOME"
open -ga Docker
# Cap the wait at 120s. A Docker that is never coming up should fail # loudly here, not leave launchd retrying an invisible compose command. for i in $(seq 1 60); do docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 && break sleep 2 done docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "docker did not become usable within 120s - not starting the stack" >&2 exit 1 }
# Keychain -> 0600 file, for containers that cannot read a Keychain. python3 scripts/tp_agent.py --write-env
# --env-file is REQUIRED, not tidiness. `env_file:` inside the compose # file supplies variables to the CONTAINER; it does not supply them to # compose's own ${...} interpolation. docker-compose.yml uses # ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?...}, which is read from the shell environment or # a file named exactly `.env` - so without this flag compose aborts # before starting anything, at login, where nobody is watching. docker compose --env-file .env.runtime -p "tp-${TP_VERSION//./-}" up -d
# The values are in the container environment now; the file is not # needed and should not outlive the command that consumed it. rm -f .env.runtime
# Becomes the long-running process launchd supervises. If the agent # dies, KeepAlive restarts it and the popups resume; the engine in the # containers is untouched either way, which is the failure mode §47 # deliberately designed for. exec python3 scripts/tp_agent.py
